newsitem.title: UK: NWE naphtha eases back with crude after upturn.
newsitem.headline: NWE naphtha eases back with crude after upturn.

text.p: NWE naphtha swung up and down on Monday as bumpy crude prices impacted with late day levels broadly steady against Friday.
August swaps were talked as high as $183-184 before settling back to $181-182.

Dealers said naphtha moved higher in the morning as crude strengthened but subsequently lost gains in the afternoon after crude tumbled on news Iraq had moved a step closer to resuming oil sales. The United Nations said talks had been finalised on a food distribution plan, the stumbling block to a resumption of exports.
Physical cargoes were pegged around $175 cif NWE with demand for N+A material still evident.

Strong Asian naphtha prices was adding a bullish undertone to the market. The Mediterranean was noticeably taking comfort from the Far Eastern interest and north African barrels were attracting high fob quotes +$2-3, dealers said.
"It makes sense to lift from the Med for Asia," one said.
